October 30, 2026 6:00am EDT[Download as PDF](https://d1io3yog0oux5.cloudfront.net/_36834363678064c5e0f064b9fa4d1062/wisdomtree/news/2026-10-30_WisdomTree_Announces_Third_Quarter_2026_814.pdf)

*Record AUM of $171.0 Billion*


*Diluted Earnings Per Share of $0.32*


*Over $13.6 Billion of Net Inflows Year-to-Date, a 13% Annualized Organic Growth Rate*


*Operating Margin Expanded by 680 bps Year over Year; or 750 bps, on an Adjusted Basis*


NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- WisdomTree, Inc. (NYSE: WT), a modern global asset manager, **** today reported financial results for the third quarter of 2026.


**$49.2 million of net income ($49.5(1) million, as adjusted).** See “Non-GAAP Financial Measurements” for a reconciliation to net income.


**$171.0 billion of ending AUM** , an increase of 5.0% from the prior quarter arising from net inflows and market appreciation.


**$4.6 billion of net inflows** , across the United States and Europe primarily driven by inflows into our fixed income, commodity and U.S. equity products.


**0.36% average advisory fee** , unchanged from the prior quarter.


**0.42% revenue yield(2)** , a 1 basis point decrease from the prior quarter due to lower transaction fees from our European ETPs and lower performance fees.


**$179.4 million of operating revenues** , an increase of 1.3% from the prior quarter due to higher average AUM, partly offset by lower transaction fees from our European ETPs and lower performance fees.


**83.0% gross margin(1)** , essentially unchanged from the prior quarter.


**41.3% operating income margin for the quarter (43.1% as adjusted)** , a 0.8 point increase (0.5 point increase, as adjusted) from the prior quarter primarily due to higher revenues.


**39.8% operating income margin year-to-date (41.8% as adjusted)** , a 6.8 point increase (7.5 point(3) increase, as adjusted) from the prior-year period. The increase primarily reflected favorable operating leverage from revenue growth, partially offset by higher intangible amortization associated with the Ceres Partners, LLC (“Ceres”) and Atlantic House Holdings Limited (“Atlantic House”) acquisitions. Adjusted operating income excludes intangible asset amortization and acquisition-related costs.


**$18.1 million aggregate principal amount of convertible senior notes due 2029 (the “2029 Notes”) retired** , for aggregate cash consideration of $32.3 million. The conversion price of the 2029 Notes was $11.82.


**$10.6 million of common stock repurchased** , representing approximately 0.5 million shares at an average repurchase price of $21.29 per share.


**$0.03 quarterly dividend declared** , payable on November 25, 2026 to stockholders of record as of the close of business on November 11, 2026.


**Update from Jarrett Lilien, WisdomTree President and COO**


“Our third quarter results reflect the continued strength and scalability of WisdomTree’s business, with record AUM of $171 billion, $4.6 billion of net inflows and meaningful contributions across our global platform. The breadth and consistency of our organic growth, coupled with expanding distribution capabilities and continued operating discipline, are driving significant operating leverage and margin expansion. As we deepen our presence in existing markets and capitalize on new opportunities across liquid alternatives, private markets and tokenization, we remain focused on executing our proven playbook: generating high-quality organic growth, scaling efficiently and translating that momentum into greater earnings power.”


**Update from Jonathan Steinberg, WisdomTree CEO**


“WisdomTree continues to evolve into a truly modern global asset manager, strategically positioned at the intersection of three powerful transformations in financial services: the democratization of investing, the convergence of public and private markets, and the tokenization of financial assets. After more than two decades of strategic reinvestment, we have built differentiated capabilities across each of these areas, and we believe the greatest opportunity lies in bringing them together into one integrated investment ecosystem. Combined with our highly efficient and scalable operating model, we believe WisdomTree is well positioned to drive sustained growth and create significant long-term value for stockholders.”

**RECENT BUSINESS DEVELOPMENTS**


Company News


- In September,


- WisdomTree completed the rebrand of Atlantic House’s fund and structured solutions business following WisdomTree’s recent acquisition of Atlantic House in May 2026;
- WisdomTree and MoonPay entered into a strategic agreement to expand U.S. investor access to tokenized funds, including the WisdomTree Treasury Money Market Digital Fund (WTGXX), and to support stablecoin reserves by making WTGXX more accessible to everyday investors through MoonPay; and
- WisdomTree introduced WisdomTree Onchain™, bringing its tokenized funds, onchain infrastructure and platforms for individual and institutional investors under one name.


- In September and October, WisdomTree won the following awards:


- Luba Spear was named “CMO of the Year” at the 2026 Wealth Management Industry Awards;
- four WisdomTree leaders were recognized on INvolve’s 2026 ‘Heroes Role Model Lists supported by YouTube;’
- the WisdomTree Enhanced Commodity UCITS ETF (WCOA) was the winner in the Commodity ETFs category at the Swiss ETF Awards 2026;
- received the “M&A Deal of the Year” award for our acquisition of Ceres Partners, LLC at the 2026 Asset Management STAR Awards North America.


- In October,


- WisdomTree and BitGo entered into an agreement to bring tokenized Treasury yield, liquidity and collateral capabilities to institutional investors directly on the BitGo platform. Eligible BitGo clients can access WTGXX without leaving the platform, putting idle cash to work while maintaining 24/7 liquidity and settlement capabilities; and
- WisdomTree and Return Stacked® ETFs entered into a strategic relationship to deliver co-branded, capital-efficient model portfolios through the Quorus implementation platform. The collaboration combines WisdomTree’s portfolio construction expertise with Return Stacked ETFs’ institutional-style diversifying strategies, helping financial advisors integrate alternative sources of return alongside core stock and bond exposures through a scalable portfolio framework.


Product News


- In August, September and October, WisdomTree launched the following products:


- In the U.S., we launched the WisdomTree Efficient Long/Short U.S. SmallCap Equity Fund (WSLS) and the WisdomTree Global Alpha Fund (WTAL), both powered by AlphaBeta and listed on the Texas Stock Exchange (TXSE).
- During the same period, in Europe, we launched the WisdomTree Enhanced Commodity UCITS ETF – GBP Hedged (WCOM), WisdomTree Physical Silver – EUR Daily Hedged (AGSE), WisdomTree Physical Silver – GBP Daily Hedged (PAGP), WisdomTree Defined Return Autocallable EUR Active UCITS ETF (DRTN) and WisdomTree Defensive Defined Return Autocallable EUR Active UCITS ETF (DRTD). The latter two ETFs – the first actively managed autocallable ETFs in Europe – leverage the investment team that joined WisdomTree through the Atlantic House acquisition. These ETFs are listed on major European exchanges, including the London Stock Exchange, Börse Xetra and Borsa Italiana. We also launched the WisdomTree Tail Risk Fund.

**QUARTERLY HIGHLIGHTS**


**Operating Revenues**


- Operating revenues increased 1.3% from the second quarter of 2026 due to higher average AUM, partly offset by lower transaction fees from our European ETPs and lower performance fees. Operating revenues increased 42.8% from the third quarter of 2025 due to higher average AUM, a higher average advisory fee, revenues arising from the Ceres and Atlantic House acquisitions and increased other revenues from our European listed ETPs.
- Our average advisory fee was 0.36% for the second and third quarters of 2026 and 0.35% for the third quarter of 2025.


**Operating Expenses**


- Operating expenses were essentially unchanged from the second quarter of 2026.
- Operating expenses increased 31.6% from the third quarter of 2025 primarily due to higher incentive compensation and headcount, as well as increased fund management and administration expenses, intangible asset amortization related to the Ceres and Atlantic House acquisitions and third-party distribution fees, partly offset by lower acquisition-related costs.


**Other Income/(Expenses)**


- Interest expense decreased 9.0% from the second quarter of 2026, reflecting a lower level of debt outstanding. Interest expense increased 59.7% from the third quarter of 2025, reflecting a higher level of debt outstanding and higher interest rates.
- Interest income decreased 42.5% and 54.1% from the second quarter of 2026 and the third quarter of 2025, respectively, reflecting a lower level of interest earning assets following recent debt retirements and stock repurchases.
- Contingent consideration related to the Ceres acquisition decreased from $15.8 million on June 30, 2026 to $13.7 million at September 30, 2026, resulting in a $2.1 million gain on remeasurement recognized during the third quarter of 2026.
- Other losses and gains, net, was a loss of $0.04 million for the third quarter of 2026. Gains and losses generally arise on our financial instruments and investments owned, as well as from the sale of gold and cryptocurrency earned from advisory fees paid by our physically-backed gold and crypto ETPs, foreign exchange fluctuations and miscellaneous items.


**Income Taxes**


- Our effective income tax rate for the third quarter of 2026 was 23.7%, resulting in income tax expense of $15.3 million. The effective tax rate differs from the U.S. federal statutory rate of 21.0% primarily due to non-deductible executive compensation and state taxes, partly offset by a reduction in the capital loss valuation allowance.
- Our adjusted effective income tax rate for the third quarter of 2026 was 24.7%(1).


**NINE MONTH HIGHLIGHTS**


- Operating revenues increased 49.0% as compared to 2025 due to higher average AUM, a higher average advisory fee, revenues arising from the Ceres and Atlantic House acquisitions and increased other revenues from our European listed ETPs.
- Operating expenses increased 34.0% as compared to 2025 primarily due to higher incentive compensation and headcount, as well as increased fund management and administration expenses, third-party distribution fees and intangible asset amortization arising from the Ceres and Atlantic House acquisitions.
- Significant items reported in other income/(expense) in 2026 include: an increase in interest expense of 103.1% due to a higher level of debt outstanding and higher interest rates; a decrease in interest income of 4.6% reflecting a lower level of interest earning assets following recent debt retirements and stock repurchases; a remeasurement gain of $4.4 million on British pounds held to complete the Atlantic House acquisition, net gains on our financial instruments owned of $2.0 million, net losses on our investments of $0.4 million and $0.6 million of foreign currency remeasurement gains on U.S. dollars held by foreign subsidiaries. Gains and losses also generally arise from the sale of gold earned on advisory fees paid by our physically-backed gold ETPs, other foreign exchange fluctuations and miscellaneous items.
- Our effective income tax rate for 2026 was 35.1%, resulting in an income tax expense of $38.1 million. The effective tax rate differs from the federal statutory rate of 21.0% primarily due to non-deductible amounts associated with the repurchase of convertible notes.

**About WisdomTree**


WisdomTree is a modern global asset manager with capabilities across public markets, private markets, tokenization and onchain finance. We offer a diverse suite of exchange-traded products, models and solutions, private market investments and blockchain-enabled products and services, helping investors shape their financial future and financial professionals grow their businesses. Through WisdomTree Onchain™, we combine tokenized investment products, infrastructure and distribution capabilities into an integrated financial services platform serving retail and institutional investors.


WisdomTree currently has approximately $175.0 billion in assets under management globally, inclusive of assets managed by Ceres as of the last reportable period.

**NON-GAAP FINANCIAL MEASUREMENTS**


In an effort to provide additional information regarding our results as determined by GAAP, we also disclose certain non-GAAP information which we believe provides useful and meaningful information. Our management reviews these non-GAAP financial measurements when evaluating our financial performance and results of operations; therefore, we believe it is useful to provide information with respect to these non-GAAP measurements so as to share this perspective of management. Non-GAAP measurements do not have any standardized meaning, do not replace nor are they superior to GAAP financial measurements and are unlikely to be comparable to similar measures presented by other companies. These non-GAAP financial measurements should be considered in the context with our GAAP results. The non-GAAP financial measurements contained in this press release include the following:


**Adjusted Operating Income, Operating Expenses, Income Before Income Taxes, Income Tax Expense, Net Income and Diluted Earnings per Share**


We disclose adjusted operating income, operating expenses, income before income taxes, income tax expense, net income and diluted earnings per share as non-GAAP financial measurements in order to report our results exclusive of items that are non-recurring or not core to our operating business. We believe presenting these non-GAAP financial measurements provides investors with a consistent way to analyze our performance. These non-GAAP financial measurements exclude the following:


***Gains or losses on financial instruments owned:*** We account for our financial instruments owned as trading securities, which requires these instruments to be measured at fair value with gains and losses reported in net income. We exclude these items when calculating our non-GAAP financial measurements as the gains and losses introduce earnings volatility and are not core to our operating business.


***Foreign currency remeasurement gains and losses on U.S. dollars held by foreign subsidiaries* :** GAAP requires account balances to be remeasured into an entity’s functional currency, with resulting gains and losses reported in net income. Foreign subsidiaries holding U.S. dollars remeasure these balances into their functional currencies and recognize the gains and losses. Also excluded are remeasurement gains on British pounds held to complete the Atlantic House acquisition. We exclude remeasurement effects from our non-GAAP financial measures, as they introduce earnings volatility, are not core to our operations and arise from balances denominated in our reporting currency.


***Tax windfalls and shortfalls upon vesting of stock-based compensation awards:*** GAAP requires the recognition of tax windfalls and shortfalls within income tax expense. These items arise upon the vesting of stock-based compensation awards and the magnitude is directly correlated to the number of awards vesting/exercised, as well as the difference between the price of our stock on the date the award was granted and the date the award vested or was exercised. We exclude these items when calculating our non-GAAP financial measurements as they introduce earnings volatility and are not core to our operating business.


***Remeasurement of contingent consideration arising from the Ceres acquisition:*** On October 1, 2025, we completed the Ceres acquisition for aggregate consideration consisting of (i) $275 million in cash payable at closing, subject to customary post-closing adjustments and (ii) contingent consideration of up to $225 million, payable in 2030, contingent upon Ceres achieving a compound annual growth rate in revenues of 12% to 22% during the measurement period of January 1, 2025 through December 31, 2029. GAAP requires contingent consideration to be re-measured each reporting period with changes in fair value reported in net income. We exclude changes in fair value of contingent consideration when calculating our non-GAAP financial measurements as these items are not core to our operating business.


***Other items:*** Amortization of intangible assets, changes in deferred tax asset valuation allowance, imputed interest on our payable to Gold Bullion Holdings (Jersey) Limited (“GBH”), gains and losses recognized on our investments, losses related to convertible notes transactions and acquisition-related costs are excluded when calculating our non-GAAP financial measurements.


**Adjusted Effective Income Tax Rate**


We disclose our adjusted effective income tax rate as a non-GAAP financial measurement in order to report our effective income tax rate exclusive of items that are non-recurring or not core to our operating business. We believe reporting our adjusted effective income tax rate provides investors with a consistent way to analyze our income taxes. Our adjusted effective income tax rate is calculated by dividing adjusted income tax expense by adjusted income before income taxes. See above for information regarding the items that are excluded.


**Gross Margin and Gross Margin Percentage**


We disclose our gross margin and gross margin percentage as non-GAAP financial measurements because we believe they provide investors with a consistent way to analyze the amount we retain after paying third-party service providers to operate our ETPs. These measures also assist us in analyzing the profitability of our products. We define gross margin as total adjusted operating revenues less fund management and administration expenses. Gross margin percentage is calculated as gross margin divided by total adjusted operating revenues.
